rv.q: Pig Heart Boy is still a fascinating and entertaining production, filled with impressive performances and wonderful stage effects.
All-in-all, a great show with a stellar cast and company who have created an excellent production of a great novel.
I definitely recommend a visit to the Playhouse to go see it.

There’s a poignant message at its core, but it’s muddied by tonal and temporal inconsistencies, clunky characterisations, boar-ingly slow-paced monologues, and an array of frustrating creative choices.

cn.t: Blackman's adaptation engages with thought-provoking ethical questions about xenotransplantation, holding attention with humor and heart. Critics find it absorbing and challenging, though one notes its modest scale.
